Serve answers agent index search for the pg store from a warm process:
it holds [serve].workers database connections, the query embedder (its
model loaded once) and the reranker's client, on a Unix socket
([serve].socket, else index.sock beside index.db). A search uses it when
it answers and runs cold otherwise, through the same code, so the answer
is the same; it runs cold too when the server is another build of agent
or runs another configuration (its fingerprint), and says why. search
--cold skips it. Serve runs until it is stopped (Ctrl-C); run it in a
session of its own.

With [embedder].endpoint, queries are embedded by that server and on the
CPU when it doesn't answer (a failed server is asked again after
[embedder].recheck_s); a search says when the CPU did it. --status asks
the running server for its health: its configuration and how each
embedding server has done.

Usage:
  agent index serve [flags]

Examples:
  agent index serve
  agent index serve --config tune/rerank50.toml
  agent index serve --status

Flags:
      --config string   The index configuration (TOML; default: AGENT_INDEX_CONFIG, else ~/.config/gomuxai/index.toml, else built-in defaults)
  -h, --help            help for serve
      --json            Print the status as JSON
      --status          Ask the running server for its health

Global Flags:
      --backend string          Backend for spawn or adopt: claude, aider, agy, or shell (spawn requires it or --backend-config; adopt auto-detects)
      --backend-config string   JSON file defining a custom backend (or app settings); pass it again to status/wait/watch for agents spawned with it
  -q, --quiet                   Don't print hints (results and errors still print)
      --termd-ns string         g3d-termd namespace (default: agents; never default or wall)
